# function: encode

Renders a map of strings in the dotenv format, one `KEY=value` line per entry, sorted by key. Values are written unquoted when possible, otherwise single or double quoted, so that `decode` and the data sources read back exactly the same value (variable references like `$VAR` are not expanded).

Keys may only contain letters, digits, underscores and dots. Values that contain a single quote or a line break *and* a literal `\n` or `\r` sequence can not be represented in the dotenv format and cause an error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Generate a .env file, e.g. for docker compose
resource "local_file" "env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/generated.env"
  content = provider::dotenv::encode({
    DATABASE_HOST = aws_db_instance.example.address
    DATABASE_PORT = tostring(aws_db_instance.example.port)
    GREETING      = "Hello World"
  })
}

# Result:
# DATABASE_HOST=example.abc123.eu-central-1.rds.amazonaws.com
# DATABASE_PORT=5432
# GREETING='Hello World'
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
encode(entries map of string) string
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `entries` (Map of String) Entries to render
